title: Although It Is True That: Si Bien and the Boom

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si bien* "although it is true that" from B2 Unit 8. It is formal, it takes the indicative, and the clause that follows says what matters more. Literary history is full of contrasts: what the Boom was, and what came after it.

items.spanish: Si bien casi todos los autores del Boom eran hombres, hoy muchas escritoras tienen lectores en todo el mundo.
items.english: Although almost all the Boom authors were men, today many women writers have readers all over the world.

items.spanish: Mariana Enríquez, si bien escribe terror, habla de problemas reales de Argentina.
items.english: Mariana Enríquez, although she writes horror, speaks about real problems in Argentina.

items.spanish: Si bien Distancia de rescate es una novela corta, tuvo mucho éxito en el extranjero.
items.english: Although Distancia de rescate is a short novel, it was very successful abroad.

items.spanish: Si bien Zambra escribe sobre su infancia, no cuenta una autobiografía.
items.english: Although Zambra writes about his childhood, he does not tell an autobiography.

sections.content: *Si bien* goes at the start of the sentence or between commas, and it never takes *que*. For "even if" (a possibility) use *aunque* + subjunctive, not *si bien*.
